title: Find Duplicate Files
statement:
Write `dupes.sh DIR`: find the regular files under `DIR` (recursively) that have **identical content**.

- Print one line per group of 2 or more identical files: their paths **relative to `DIR`**, sorted, joined with ` | `.
- Sort the groups by their first path.
- Files with the same name but different content are not duplicates. Empty files are duplicates of each other.
- Paths may contain spaces (you can assume no newlines in names).
- No `DIR` argument: print an error and exit non-zero. No duplicates: print nothing.

```
$ dupes.sh photos
a.jpg | backup/a copy.jpg
notes.txt | old/notes.txt | old/notes2.txt
```
starter_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# dupes.sh DIR
for f in $(find $1 -type f); do
  md5sum $f
done | sort | uniq -w32 -d
harness:
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; mkdir d; echo a > d/x; echo b > d/y
  run_solution d
  if [[ $status == 0 && -z $out ]]; then pass "no duplicates: no output"
  else fail "no duplicates: no output" "status=$status stdout=[$out]"; fi
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; mkdir d; echo same > d/a.txt; echo same > d/b.txt; echo other > d/c.txt
  run_solution d
  expect_eq "one pair" "a.txt | b.txt" "$out"
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; mkdir -p d/old; echo n > d/notes.txt; echo n > d/old/notes.txt; echo n > d/old/notes2.txt
  run_solution d
  expect_eq "a group of three across directories" "notes.txt | old/notes.txt | old/notes2.txt" "$out"
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; mkdir d; echo 1 > d/z1; echo 1 > d/a1; echo 2 > d/m2; echo 2 > d/b2
  run_solution d
  expect_eq "several groups, sorted by first path" $'a1 | z1\nb2 | m2' "$out"
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; mkdir -p "d/my photos"; echo pic > "d/my photos/a copy.jpg"; echo pic > d/a.jpg
  run_solution d
  expect_eq "paths with spaces" "a.jpg | my photos/a copy.jpg" "$out"
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; mkdir -p d/x d/y; echo 1 > d/x/same-name; echo 2 > d/y/same-name; : > d/e1; : > d/e2
  run_solution d
  expect_eq "same name isn't enough; empty files are duplicates" "e1 | e2" "$out"
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"
  run_solution
  if [[ $status != 0 ]]; then pass "no argument is an error"; else fail "no argument is an error" "exited 0"; fi
)
reference_solution:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# dupes.sh DIR
dir=${1:?usage: dupes.sh DIR}
cd -- "$dir" || exit 1      # work relative to DIR, so printed paths are relative

declare -A groups=()        # content hash -> newline-separated paths
while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do
  hash=$(sha256sum < "$path")
  hash=${hash%% *}
  path=${path#./}
  groups[$hash]+="$path"$'\n'
done < <(find . -type f -print0)

for hash in "${!groups[@]}"; do
  mapfile -t files < <(printf '%s' "${groups[$hash]}" | sort)
  (( ${#files[@]} > 1 )) || continue
  line=${files[0]}
  for f in "${files[@]:1}"; do line+=" | $f"; done
  printf '%s\n' "$line"
done | sort
hints: Group by a content hash: `sha256sum < "$path"` prints the hash (then `-`). Keep everything before the first space.
Use an associative array from hash to a newline-separated list of paths, and append with `groups[$hash]+="$path"$'\n'`.
`cd` into the directory and run `find . -type f -print0`, then strip the leading `./` to get relative paths.
`mapfile -t files < <(... | sort)` turns a sorted list back into an array.
discussion:
**Grouping by a hash of the content** turns an O(n²) "compare every pair" problem into O(n) hashing plus a lookup. It's the same idea behind deduplicating backups, git's object store and content-addressed caches.

- **Same name ≠ same content, and different names can be identical.** Only content matters, which is why the key is a hash.
- **Collisions:** with SHA-256, an accidental collision is not a practical concern. (MD5 is fine for accidental duplicates, but don't use it where an attacker could craft collisions.) A belt-and-braces tool confirms with a byte-by-byte `cmp` before deleting anything.
- **Performance:** hashing every byte of every file is the expensive part. Real tools (`fdupes`, `rdfind`, `jdupes`) first group by **file size**, since files of different sizes can't be equal, then hash only the candidates, often hashing just the first few KB first.
- **Robust traversal again:** `find -print0` + `read -d ''`. The starter's `$(find ...)` breaks on `my photos`.
- **Deterministic output** (sorted within groups and between groups) makes the tool scriptable and testable.

**Follow-ups:** How would you add a `--size-first` optimisation? What should a "delete the duplicates" option keep, and how would you make it safe? (Hard links? A dry run?)
